To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The cross section for e + e − →hadrons above the charm threshold can be described in a charm quark model, with the ψ′′ and possibly the ψ ‴ as important ingredients.

the charm scheme, which was originally devised to explain the behaviour of σ(e + e − →hadrons) in the energy region below 3.5 GeV, can also be applied in the energy region above the charm threshold, and that the charm scheme provides a satisfactory description of σ(e +e − → hadrons ) in the energy region from 4.5 GeV to 6 GeV, which is the energy region of interest for the future LEP experiments.

the cross section for e + e − annihilation into hadrons is dominated by the contribution of the ψ resonance and its excited states, and that the cross section above the ψ resonance can be described by the contribution of ψ′ and ψ ″ resonances.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (a) What is the role of the ψ′' and ψ ‴ in the region between 4.5 and 6 GeV/c 2? (b) What is the contribution of the ψ′', ψ ‴ to the cross section above 6 GeV/ c 2? (c) How can one distinguish between the ψ′', and ψ ‴ and the continuum states?
the question of the role of charm and of the ψ meson in the annihilation of electrons and positrons above the charm threshold.

the following questions: What is the role of the ψ′ in the total e + e − →hadron cross-section above the charm threshold? What is the role, if any, of the ψ ″ in e + e − annihilation above charm? What are the contributions of the ψ ′ and the ψ ″ to the e + e − total cross-section? What are the relative contributions of ψ ′ and ψ ″ to σ (e +e −→ ψ ′ + X)?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charm scheme is a useful and promising tool for describing the annihilation process in the energy range above charm threshold.
the present data are compatible with the charm scheme, and the charm scheme is compatible with the data.
, at present, the data do not yet permit to decide whether or not the ψ′' is a genuine radial excitation of the ψ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the charm scheme is able to describe the experimental data on σ (e +e − → hadrons), both below and above the threshold, with an acceptable accuracy, and that it can also be used for a prediction for the cross-section above the threshold, which is in a good qualitative and in some cases also in a good quantitative agreement with experiment.
the charm scheme provides a reasonable description of the behaviour of σ above charm threshold.
the charm scheme, in spite of its shortcomings, is able to describe the data in the energy range 4.0–5.0 GeV with reasonable accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the behaviour of σ(e + e − →hadrons) above charm threshold can be described in the charm scheme, if we take into account the contributions from higher resonances.
the ψ ′ is the most important state above charm threshold, with the ψ ″ and ψ ‴ playing minor roles.
the charm scheme is able to account for the experimental data on e + e − →hadrons in the region above the threshold for charm production, provided the ψ ′ is taken into account.
